title: Propagation of coefficient data through finite tests and smooth pullback
statement:
Let $X\hookrightarrow Z$ be a reduced closed finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme in a smooth scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix $a\in X$, $H_0=H_X(a)$ [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant], a neighbourhood on which $H_X\le_{\rm lex}H_0$, and supplied regular Hilbert coefficient data on a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$ [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum], with jet bound $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ (vacuous for an empty vertex list). For the positive weights $m_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|$, let $b$ be a positive common multiple and $I=\sum(c_{i\gamma}^{b/m_{i\gamma}})$, or $(I,b)=(0,1)$ for an empty vertex list [pqf-def-coherent] [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. Write $e:U\to Z$ for the supplied datum\textquotesingle s etale chart, $a_U\in U$ for its distinguished point, and $j:N\hookrightarrow U$ for its coefficient support. There exists one open $V\subseteq U$ containing $a_U$ such that all assertions below hold for the initial ambient $V$, embedded scheme $X_V=X\times_ZV$, coefficient support $N_V=j^{-1}(V)$, and the restrictions of $I$ and every coefficient to $N_V$. All finite test sequences and their clauses start on this same restricted chart. Start with empty ordered test boundary. A finite test sequence allows (i) a blowup of a smooth center in the retaining-level locus, having normal crossings with the boundary, with strict transform of $X,N$ and ideal transform $e^{-b}\sigma^*I$; (ii) product with $\mathbf A^1$, using ordinary pullbacks and appending the zero section; (iii) blowup of the intersection of two distinct boundary components, using ordinary pullbacks of $X,N,I$. Each blowup retains the ordered strict transforms and appends the new exceptional divisor [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform] [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation].
For every such finite sequence of length $s$, all these transforms are defined. If $\ell_j$ is the number of line products in its prefix of length $j\le s$, then
$$\operatorname{cosupp}(I_j,b)=\{x\in X_j:H_{X_j}(x)=\Lambda^{\ell_j}H_0\}$$
as subsets of the current ambient scheme. Every boundary component is transverse to the current $N_j$, its equation being a coordinate on $N_j$ in coordinates $(W,Z)$ adapted to the coefficient datum. At the retaining-level points the transformed coefficient data satisfy the same five division and Jacobian conditions; for (iii) the coefficient functions are ordinary pullbacks, and the Hilbert--Samuel level is unchanged, while (ii) replaces it by $\Lambda H$. At every prefix the two loci permit exactly the same next smooth centers, with the same labelled boundary; hence the marked datum is a presentation in the finite-test sense. Empty cosupport and centers which remove a component are allowed.
For a smooth map $f:Z_1\to V$ of constant relative dimension $r\ge0$ and $X_1=X_V\times_VZ_1$, one has $H_{X_1}(y)=\Lambda^rH_{X_V}(g(y))$, where $g:X_1\to X_V$ is the cartesian projection. The pulled-back coefficient data and ideal are a presentation of $\Lambda^rH_0$, with the same finite-test assertions. Moreover $\Lambda^r$ preserves and reflects lexicographic equality and inequalities of sequences. These assertions commute with open restriction and hold separately on each relative-dimension piece; they do not identify unsummed numerical levels for $r>0$.

source.place: ILO VIII 2.3.11--2.3.13, pp.93--94; BM 1997 Definition 6.2, formulas (6.1), Theorems 7.20--7.21; BMT 5.2, 6.2--6.3. Boundary/test induction and smooth base change from old proof steps 5,7. No Stacks tag states this finite-test propagation theorem.

proof.text: Put $L_j=\Lambda^{\ell_j}H_0$ and let $S_j$ be the coefficient order locus. Induct on prefixes with: $H_{X_j}\le_{\rm lex}L_j$ everywhere, $S_j=\{H_{X_j}=L_j\}$, the five conditions on $S_j$, the coefficient-power identity for $I_j$, and the labelled coordinate boundary. Retain also the following boundary history, including points below $L_j$. A boundary germ is either a free-coordinate germ, obtained from line zero sections by boundary charts over an earlier $X$, or lies over a center of an earlier type-(i) blowup. In the latter case retain its transformed generators, their supported multiplication identities, the identities (4),(5), and their pure-transverse degree-$d_i$ values from that earlier $S$-point, as constructed in steps 2--5. The history is empty initially. The supplied datum gives the upper bound and conditions, and [lem-trf-common-power-hilbert-marking] gives the initial cosupport identity and coherence, including the empty vertex convention. The supplied jet bound is $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$, as required by the marking theorem and by the degree-$m$ use of (5) in step 10.

proof.text: Here is the information stored at a source point $a\in S_j$. Write $A_i=\operatorname{in}_{d_i}f_i$. The quotient supports $\Delta_i$ impose conditions only on transverse exponents, since all vertices have zero $W$ components. For each degree prefix, arrange its homogeneous division matrix by increasing complementary-variable degree. It is block triangular, with diagonal blocks the division matrices for the restrictions of $A_i$ to the prefix essential transverse variables (all other variables set to zero). Thus these pure-transverse forms have homogeneous division for every prefix. By (3), each $Z^\beta f_i$ has a supported expansion $\sum q_h f_h$. Store these identities for all $i,\beta$ (not just ideal generation). Conditions (4),(5) are identities of series at $a$, not just vanishing of their values at $a$; they are stored too. All source series will be substituted through parameters vanishing at this same source point. No translation of an arbitrary infinite series to a different point is being used. The homogeneous division and filtration estimates used here are those of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division].

proof.text: For a type-(i) blowup the current center lies in $S_j$, so [lem-trf-marked-controlled-blowup-charts] supplies the smooth ambient and coefficient transforms, regular controlled ideal, and labelled transverse boundary. [lem-trf-common-power-hilbert-marking] gives $H_{X_{j+1}}\le_{\rm lex}L_j$ over the center, equality exactly on the controlled cosupport, the five conditions there, and exclusion of equality from charts missing $N_{j+1}$. Outside the center nothing changes. Its regular coefficients are $c'_{i\gamma}=e^{|\gamma|-d_i}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$ and their powers generate $e^{-b}\sigma^*I_j$. This proves the ordinary part of the invariant with $L_{j+1}=L_j$. To retain the additional history over the entire exceptional fibre, including lower-level points, use the constructions in the next two steps. Removed components and empty charts are exactly those permitted in the chart theorem.

proof.text:
Fix $a$ in this center, write $P=(Y,Z)$, and work on a chart meeting $N'$: $Y_h=e$, $Y_k=e(\eta_k+U_k)$, $Z=eZ'$, with unchanged center parameters. [lem-trf-coordinate-blowup-division-generators] says that the actual saturated ideal is generated by $f_i'=e^{-d_i}\sigma^*f_i$, at all points of the chart over $a$. For the stored expansion $Z^\beta f_i=\sum q_h f_h$, its $P$-order is $v=d_i+|\beta|$. The same node gives $\operatorname{ord}_Pq_h\ge v-d_h$. Hence
$$(Z')^\beta f_i'=\sum_h(e^{d_h-v}\sigma^*q_h)f_h'$$
has regular coefficients. They retain support $\Delta_h$, since only coefficient variables were mixed and the transverse variables were scaled without translation. These are supported multiplication identities on the whole fibre over $a$, whether or not its points retain order. Subsequent ordinary substitutions of coefficient variables preserve them. Source parameters still vanish at $a$, so all substituted series converge in the current Taylor ring. These identities are stronger than the equality-locus conditions used in the returned proof. On charts missing $N\prime$, the same node still gives generation of the saturated ideal; the supported identities are needed only on charts meeting $N\prime$.

proof.text: On the same charts, differentiation gives $g_j'=e^{-1}\sigma^*g_j$ and $\partial_{Z'_k}g_j'=\sigma^*(\partial_{Z_k}g_j)$. Thus (4) holds as an ideal-membership identity near $N'$ with the source invertible Jacobian on the exceptional fibre, without assuming equality of orders. Likewise $\partial_{Z'^\ell}^{\delta}f_i'=e^{|\delta|-d_i}\sigma^*(\partial_{Z^\ell}^{\delta}f_i)$ lies in $(Z'^\ell)$ after inverting $e$. It is regular and $(Z'^\ell)$ is $e$-saturated, so the membership holds before inversion. This retains (5). On $e=0$ the degree-$d_i$ pure-$Z'$ part is precisely $A_i(0,Z')$: in $c'_{i\gamma}=e^{|\gamma|-d_i}\sigma^*c_{i\gamma}$, the terms with $|\gamma|=d_i$ evaluate at $a$, and higher transverse degrees vanish. Low coefficients may survive and lower the order. In charts missing $N'$, the same derivative identities evaluated on the projective transverse direction give the corresponding nonzero constant rows; the first nonzero transverse block forces an order drop. This records the source of those rows for step 10. Taylor compatibility and contraction to regular models use [lem-trf-implicit-taylor-coordinate-calculus].

proof.text: For type (ii), keep $Z$ transverse and append a free coordinate $t$ to $W$. The line-product assertion of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] takes ordinary pullbacks of the coefficients and retains their division and Jacobian conditions. Its formula for the Hilbert function is one summation. The Taylor-jet comparison of [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control] interprets this formula as the extended function at every scheme point, including a generic point of a fibre: one retains the relative Taylor variable even there. Thus the new level is $\Lambda L_j$ and the coefficient order locus equals its equality locus. The common-power assertion identifies this order locus with the cosupport of the ordinarily pulled-back ideal. Old boundary equations remain $W$ coordinates and the appended zero section has equation $t$; these are distinct coordinates on $N_j\times\mathbf A^1$. This gives all induction assertions with $\ell_{j+1}=\ell_j+1$. Ordinary pullback also retains every stored identity. The new zero section is a free-coordinate boundary until a later nontrivial type-(i) center is encountered. The upper bound follows from smooth pullback and order reflection of summation (step 13).

proof.text: For a type-(iii) test, trace the germ of its two boundary components back through the prefix. Initially there is no boundary. A line introduces an independent zero-section coordinate; a boundary blowup replaces two such coordinates by $e,eu$ and introduces another coordinate component. As long as no type-(i) exceptional locus is encountered, all these charts are products over the preceding $X$: their coordinate rings are $A[e,u,\ldots]$ over its affine ring $A$. Thus this case is smooth over that earlier $X$, with the same accumulated relative dimension, and cannot create a new retaining-level point over a lower-level point. If a type-(i) exceptional locus is encountered, its center was in the earlier $S$. Choose the last such type-(i) operation affecting the germ. Every intervening type-(i) map is an isomorphism at the germ, and the remaining operations are line products and substitutions in boundary coordinates. The certificates of steps 4--5 therefore apply over that earlier $S$-point, even if the current image is below $L_j$. This dichotomy is preserved when the new exceptional component is appended. It does not assert that the present boundary intersection lies in $S_j$.

source.place: VIII 2.3.8--2.3.17, printed pp.93--95: referral to BM/BMT, not a proof of coefficient transforms; agent-written boundary-history and supported-division argument

proof.text: Write the current two boundary equations as $W_1,W_2$. [lem-trf-permissible-coordinate-chart] gives the two charts $W_1=e,W_2=eu$ and $W_2=e,W_1=ev$, with unchanged transverse variables. Thus $N'=Z=0$ is the smooth cartesian pullback and the surviving boundary equations and $e$ are distinct coordinates on it. Use total pullback of the ideal of $X$ and ordinary pullback of all $c_{i\gamma}$, with no exceptional division. For a history germ of the second kind in step 7, the ideal is generated by the pulled-back $f_i$: this was true on the entire earlier type-(i) fibre by step 4 and ideal generation survives ordinary pullback. Identities (4),(5) survive these coefficient-variable substitutions identically. At a new coefficient-order point all low-order terms vanish. The pure-transverse degree-$d_i$ forms are still the earlier $A_i(0,Z)$, including when orders at the intermediate image had dropped. The block-triangular matrix argument of step 2 now gives (1),(2) for every prefix at this new point. No assertion of the formal criterion over a non-equality source point is used.

source.place: VIII 2.3.8--2.3.17, printed pp.93--95: referral to BM/BMT, not a proof of coefficient transforms; agent-written boundary-history and supported-division argument

proof.text: It remains to prove (3) at such a new point; ideal generation alone would not suffice. The pulled-back identities of step 4 express every $Z^\beta f_i$ as a supported sum. Multiplication by any coefficient-variable monomial preserves support because $\Delta_h$ has no restriction in those variables. Thus polynomial multiples of the $f_i$ are supported sums. At the new order point step 8 supplies the homogeneous basis hypothesis of [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division]. Its supported-sum space is closed in the maximal-ideal topology. Approximate any formal multiplier by polynomials; continuity of multiplication and that closedness show that every element of the generated ideal is a supported sum. Since this generated ideal is the actual total-pullback Taylor ideal, (3) holds. Together with step 8 and the identities of step 5, this proves all five conditions at every new coefficient-order point, including points above a current image outside $S_j$. The same division theorem now gives its Hilbert function $H_D=L_j$. For a free-coordinate germ, the conclusion instead follows directly from the smooth product description in step 7.

source.place: VIII 2.3.8--2.3.17, printed pp.93--95: referral to BM/BMT, not a proof of coefficient transforms; agent-written boundary-history and supported-division argument

proof.text: We also need the bound on the whole neighbourhood. At a history point of $N'$ outside the new order locus, take the first degree block with a dropping generator, and let $m<d_0$ be a least degree of a drop in that block. Earlier blocks retain their orders; their pure-transverse forms and the triangular matrix argument give prefix division. Up through degree $m$, their supported columns number exactly the monomials of $D$ in those degrees, since later vertices have degree at least $d_0$. They give $H(t)\le H_D(t)$ for $t\le m$. Identity (5) makes the degree-$m$ form of a dropping generator have zero coefficients on the prefix diagram. It is a nonzero remainder, hence independent of those columns by homogeneous uniqueness. Thus $H(m)<H_D(m)$, so $H<_{\rm lex}L_j$. Away from $N'$, use the first nonzero transverse block in step 5: a derivative of order $d_i-1$ is a unit, forcing a drop in that block. If an earlier block already drops use it instead. Earlier retained transverse blocks have zero projective direction, so the identical prefix-column count applies. In a chart whose pivot is transverse, that pivot belongs to a dropping block; all earlier retained transverse variables remain available. This excludes equality off $N'$ and gives the same strict bound there. These are counts in the actual generated Taylor ideal, using [lem-trf-homogeneous-continuous-formal-division], not a claim that the Hilbert function at a lower-level image was unchanged.

source.place: VIII 2.3.8--2.3.17, printed pp.93--95: referral to BM/BMT, not a proof of coefficient transforms; agent-written boundary-history and supported-division argument

proof.text: Steps 7--10 show $H\le_{\rm lex}L_j$ globally after type (iii), and equality exactly at the new coefficient-order locus on $N'$. The product- and sum-order formulas in [lem-trf-logarithmic-differential-transform] identify that locus with cosupport: $\operatorname{ord}(c^{b/m})=(b/m)\operatorname{ord}c$ and the order of a finitely generated sum is the minimum. Their powers are exactly the ordinary pullback of $I_j$. The boundary and all historical identities have been retained, so the strengthened induction closes, with $L_{j+1}=L_j$. In particular, before applying common-power marking to a later type-(i) center, the five conditions are available at every point of that center. If its full datum requires a pointwise, rather than lexicographic, upper neighbourhood, [lem-trf-extended-hilbert-local-upper-bound] gives one at each such equality point; its finite-value and finite-module hypotheses are supplied for these Taylor ideals in that node and [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control]. This is a local application around the center, not deletion of lower-level boundary points from the invariant.

proof.text: The three cases complete induction for every finite prefix, and include the empty schemes arising from component removal. At any prefix, containment of a proposed next smooth center in one of the two equal subsets is equivalent to containment in the other. The ambient scheme and ordered boundary are the same, so its normal-crossings condition is literally the same condition. The transform constructions have just been supplied for every allowed next test. These are exactly the recursive finite-depth predicates in [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation]; quantifying over all depths proves the presentation assertion, including prefixes with empty cosupport.

proof.text: For any two sequences $F,G$, if $n$ is their first differing index, their partial sums agree below $n$ and their difference at $n$ is $F(n)-G(n)$. Consequently $\Lambda$ preserves the first differing index and the direction of its inequality. It is injective: recover $F(0)$ from its zeroth partial sum and $F(n+1)$ by subtracting consecutive partial sums. Iterating gives preservation and reflection of equality, strict lexicographic inequality and non-strict lexicographic inequality for $\Lambda^r$, including $r=0$. These are the summation and lexicographic conventions of [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant].

proof.text: Let $f:Z_1\to Z$ be smooth of constant relative dimension $r$. By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], locally $f$ factors through an etale map to $\mathbf A_Z^r$; the number of free coordinates equals $r$ on this piece. Apply the free-variable and etale Taylor comparisons of [lem-trf-jet-diagram-hilbert-control]: the Taylor ideal of $X_1$ is obtained by coefficient-field extension and adjoining $r$ free variables, so $H_{X_1}(y)=\Lambda^r H_X(f(y))$. Step 13 reflects equality, hence the inverse image of the original level is exactly the level $\Lambda^rH_0$. The coefficient and residue-extension clauses of [lem-trf-formal-coefficient-transform-criterion] give the pulled-back coefficients, homogeneous division bases and unchanged transverse Jacobians. This yields supplied coefficient data with the same weights on the smooth pullback, and the common-power ideal is its actual pullback because finite sums and powers commute with ring homomorphisms. Repeat the strengthened induction of steps 1--12 for these data on $Z_1$: the induction treats arbitrary next centers upstairs, and does not require such centers to descend to $Z$. Therefore the pulled-back datum has all finite-test assertions. Start its test boundary empty. Free-coordinate histories remain products after this base change; every later type-(i) source is an upstairs equality point, so steps 4--5 construct the same certificates there. Thus restarting the induction does carry the strengthened invariant.

proof.text: Every construction and every displayed identity is local in the ambient scheme. The etale-localization clauses of the coefficient criterion and jet comparison therefore give agreement on overlaps and under open restriction. If the relative dimension is not constant, apply the preceding argument on each relative-dimension piece. At dimension $r>0$ the asserted level is $\Lambda^rH_0$; the injectivity argument compares these summed levels and does not replace them by $H_0$.

statement_change.old_statement:
Let $X\hookrightarrow Z$ be a reduced closed finite-type $\mathbf Q$-scheme in a smooth scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme] [def-weil-closed-immersion] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Fix $a\in X$, $H_0=H_X(a)$ [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-invariant], a neighbourhood on which $H_X\le_{\rm lex}H_0$, and supplied regular Hilbert coefficient data on a smooth closed $N\hookrightarrow Z$ [def-trf-regular-hilbert-coefficient-datum], with jet bound $Q\ge\max_i d_i-1$ (vacuous for an empty vertex list). For the positive weights $m_{i\gamma}=d_i-|\gamma|$, let $b$ be a positive common multiple and $I=\sum(c_{i\gamma}^{b/m_{i\gamma}})$, or $(I,b)=(0,1)$ for an empty vertex list [pqf-def-coherent] [def-trf-marked-ideal-order]. Start with empty ordered test boundary. A finite test sequence allows (i) a blowup of a smooth center in the retaining-level locus, having normal crossings with the boundary, with strict transform of $X,N$ and ideal transform $e^{-b}\sigma^*I$; (ii) product with $\mathbf A^1$, using ordinary pullbacks and appending the zero section; (iii) blowup of the intersection of two distinct boundary components, using ordinary pullbacks of $X,N,I$. Each blowup retains the ordered strict transforms and appends the new exceptional divisor [def-nagata-global-blowup] [def-nagata-strict-transform] [def-trf-hilbert-samuel-presentation].
For every such finite sequence of length $s$, all these transforms are defined. If $\ell_j$ is the number of line products in its prefix of length $j\le s$, then
$$\operatorname{cosupp}(I_j,b)=\{x\in X_j:H_{X_j}(x)=\Lambda^{\ell_j}H_0\}$$
as subsets of the current ambient scheme. Every boundary component is transverse to the current $N_j$, its equation being a coordinate on $N_j$ in coordinates $(W,Z)$ adapted to the coefficient datum. At the retaining-level points the transformed coefficient data satisfy the same five division and Jacobian conditions; for (iii) the coefficient functions are ordinary pullbacks, and the Hilbert--Samuel level is unchanged, while (ii) replaces it by $\Lambda H$. At every prefix the two loci permit exactly the same next smooth centers, with the same labelled boundary; hence the marked datum is a presentation in the finite-test sense. Empty cosupport and centers which remove a component are allowed.
For a smooth map $f:Z_1\to Z$ of constant relative dimension $r\ge0$ and $X_1=X\times_ZZ_1$, one has $H_{X_1}(y)=\Lambda^rH_X(f(y))$. The pulled-back coefficient data and ideal are a presentation of $\Lambda^rH_0$, with the same finite-test assertions. Moreover $\Lambda^r$ preserves and reflects lexicographic equality and inequalities of sequences. These assertions commute with open restriction and hold separately on each relative-dimension piece; they do not identify unsummed numerical levels for $r>0$.
statement_change.what: The initial equality is a germ assertion and need not hold throughout the supplied etale chart U. The returned counterexample has Z=U=A^2, X=V(xy(x+y-6)), a=(0,0), N={z=0}, c0=-w^2, c1=0, c2=1, alpha=(2), Q=1, b=2: coefficient cosupport contains only the origin, whereas the retaining Hilbert level contains all three nodes. Choose one open V containing the distinguished point and restrict X, N, coefficients and every finite-test/presentation/smooth-pullback clause to V, exactly as the initial common-power lemma permits.
